LMP3.title: Eurointernational inherit LMP3 win after United’s post-race penalty
LMP3.dek: Mondini and Uboldi were promoted to the LMP3 win when a post-race time penalty dropped Falb and Rayhall’s United Ligier, first across the line, to second.

facts.v: The United #2 was given a 25-second time penalty after the flag for failing to slow enough under a full-course yellow, which gave Eurointernational the class win.

chapters.title: A third Norma and a karting graduate
text: LMP3 reached Austria with 17 cars: 14 Ligier JS P3s and three Norma M30s. The newest Norma belonged to Duqueine Engineering, which parked one of its Ligiers and entered the #7 for Borga, Droux and Schatz, a chassis that had made its only previous start in a VdeV round at Dijon. Duqueine’s other car, the #8, had a rookie in Lundberg, a 25-year-old Swede who had raced only karts and first drove the car less than a week earlier; team-mate Légeret had only been old enough to drive a car since his 16th birthday two months earlier.

Eurointernational’s #12 had Capo and Dayson in the car, and Ehrlacher came back to M.Racing - YMR’s #19 Norma fresh from his first WTCC win in Argentina. The Lahayes and Heriau arrived as class leaders in Ultimate’s #17. In practice Capitanio put Oregon Team’s Norma on top in FP1 with a 1:26.376, three tenths clear, ahead of Boyd and Jensen. Jensen then led FP2 for AT Racing on a 1:26.507, with Gachet’s Panis Barthez Ligier second, in a session full of gravel trips that included a crash which damaged the front of United’s #3 in England’s hands.

chapters.title: Droux puts the new Norma on pole
text: Droux’s 1:25.657 gave the #7 Norma pole on its first qualifying outing for Duqueine, 0.197 ahead of Jensen’s #9 AT Racing Ligier. Jensen had briefly looked to have beaten it before a final lap was cancelled for track limits. Ehrlacher, who had held provisional pole, took third in the #19 Norma on 1:26.052, with Boyd’s United #3 fourth, 0.422 off the pace, and Gachet’s Panis Barthez #16 fifth.

The class session was red-flagged for several minutes when Kaiser’s 360 Racing Ligier lost a wheel on the run to Turn 3, and the #6 started from the back of the field. Falb and Rayhall’s United #2 lined up sixth in class, Mondini’s Eurointernational #11 eighth and the championship-leading Ultimate #17 ninth, all within about 0.9s of pole.

chapters.title: Jensen leads, Rayhall charges
text: All LMP3 cars got away cleanly. Jensen led from the green light, Rayhall jumped from sixth to second in the #2 United Ligier, and pole-sitter Droux dropped to third. Rayhall pressured Jensen for a few laps, but Droux passed him on lap 12 and Mondini’s Eurointernational Ligier followed on lap 30. By the end of the hour Jensen was 14 seconds clear of Droux and 31 ahead of Mondini.

chapters.title: Fuel-only stops reshuffle the order
text: The first stops, around lap 45, changed the order. Mondini and Rayhall took fuel only while the #7 and #9 changed drivers, which put the #11 in front of the #2, #7 and #9, and the top three then barely moved through the second hour. After the next round of stops Schatz took the lead from Uboldi at Turn 1 in the #7 Norma, but held it for fewer than five laps before spinning and stopping for a long time at Turn 4. That left Uboldi 18 seconds clear of Falb in the #2, with Ricci in M.Racing - YMR’s #18 next.

chapters.title: Falb takes the lead
text: A full-course yellow, the only one of the race, was called with an hour to go for a stopped LMP2 car. After the final stops Uboldi led Falb by less than four seconds and held him off for several laps, but lost the lead after getting caught up in traffic at Turn 4. Falb then pulled away, building a gap of close to 25 seconds.

chapters.title: A late drive-through, a narrow flag
text: With the race almost over the #2 was given a drive-through penalty for abusing track limits. Falb served it and rejoined still in front, while Uboldi cut the deficit to under three seconds. Falb left the pit lane about two seconds clear and took the chequered flag less than two seconds ahead on the road. “I seem to like to turn on the drama,” he said afterwards. The result did not stand.

chapters.title: United’s double lasts a few hours
text: After the race the #2 received a 25-second time penalty, which dropped Falb and Rayhall to second and handed the win to Mondini and Uboldi in the #11 Eurointernational Ligier, 157 laps for both. It was Eurointernational’s first LMP3 win of 2017; Silverstone had gone to the United #2 and Monza to M.Racing - YMR’s Norma #19.

Cougnaud, Jung and Ricci were third in the #18 on the same lap, and championship leaders Lahaye, Lahaye and Heriau fourth in the #17. Inter Europol’s #13 was fifth, one lap down, then Jensen’s #9, which set the class fastest lap on a 1:26.406, Oregon’s #10 and RLR’s #15, both two laps down. Duqueine’s #7 finished ninth after Schatz’s spin, three laps behind, ahead of By Speed Factory’s #5 and the #8. The #4 was not classified on 150 laps, as were the #12 and #19, which managed only 44 and 41, while the #3, #6 and #16 were also not classified. The series returns to Paul Ricard on 27 August.

LMGTE.title: Griffin passes JMW to give Spirit of Race its first win of the year
LMGTE.dek: Cameron, Griffin and Scott won in Spirit of Race’s #55 Ferrari after Griffin caught and passed JMW’s Fannin late on, while Thiim’s Aston Martin beat the sister Ferrari to third.

facts.v: Bertolini’s 1:28.297 put the #51 Ferrari on pole, with Griffin’s #55 second, less than two tenths behind.

chapters.title: Six GTE cars and a new Ferrari at JMW
text: The GTE field was back to six cars after Larbre’s Corvette, a one-off at Monza, did not return. The rest of the field was unchanged apart from JMW, which swapped the retired Ferrari 458 for the 488 GTE it had taken to Le Mans, with Smith the only driver present who had raced it there. JMW had won at Monza in the 458’s final appearance, after TF Sport’s Aston Martin took the opener at Silverstone.

Practice went to the Ferraris and Proton. Cairoli’s Proton Porsche #77 was quickest in FP1 on a 1:29.728, only a few thousandths ahead of Thiim’s TF Sport Aston Martin, before Bertolini’s Spirit of Race #51 Ferrari topped FP2 with a 1:28.407, about three tenths clear of the Porsche. Turner’s Beechdean Aston Martin #99 was third. All running so far had been dry, though the forecast showed scattered storms and a growing chance of rain towards the end of the race.

chapters.title: Spirit of Race take the front row
text: Spirit of Race locked out the front row. Bertolini set the benchmark on his third flying lap, finished on 1:28.297 and stayed on top to the end of the session. Griffin’s #55 sister car was second on 1:28.476, less than two tenths away, and held the place only in the last moments after a fight with Cairoli, who took third for Proton on 1:28.606.
Cocker’s JMW Ferrari was fourth on 1:28.713 and Thiim fifth for TF Sport on 1:28.862, with Turner sixth for Beechdean on 1:28.906. All six cars were within 0.609 seconds of pole.

chapters.title: Three Ferraris at the front
text: For most of the race the GTE class was a fight among the three Ferrari 488s: the two Spirit of Race cars and JMW’s #66. The Aston Martins were quiet for much of the distance, and the Proton Porsche, third on the grid, slipped back to finish fifth.

chapters.title: Fannin’s lead lasts a few laps
text: The decisive moment came in the last half hour. At JMW’s final stop Fannin took over the #66 and left the pits with a lead of less than five seconds over the #55, now driven by Griffin. Griffin said he could see the JMW as he exited the pits and knew he was quicker. He caught Fannin patiently and passed him in traffic as Fannin struggled to lap one of the LMP3 Normas.

chapters.title: Thiim takes third late
text: Once in front, Griffin cruised to the flag well clear of the JMW. The last podium place was settled by the closing laps: Thiim attacked Giorgio Roda’s #51 Ferrari in the final half hour, passed him for third and held it to the flag despite relentless pressure from the Italian.

chapters.title: First win of the season for the #55
text: Cameron, Griffin and Scott took the first win of the season for the #55 Ferrari, 155 laps. Smith, Fannin and Cocker were second in the JMW Ferrari, ahead of Yoluc, Hankey and Thiim in the TF Sport Aston Martin, with Gianluca Roda, Giorgio Roda and Bertolini fourth in the #51 and the Proton Porsche of Ried, Camathias and Cairoli fifth, all on the winner’s lap. Howard, Gunn and Turner were sixth for Beechdean, one lap down, and Griffin set the class fastest lap on a 1:29.147. The series returns to Paul Ricard on 27 August.
